analysis.title: The AI dollar is here
key_insights: Over the last two weeks, tech stocks and the dollar have sold off sharply at the same time. The author has argued that the dollar's risk-off properties cannot be taken for granted in an AI-driven market correction.
US reliance on foreign equity inflows is historically unprecedented. These inflows currently finance the entire US current account deficit, while the equity market is highly concentrated.

The author estimates roughly 90% of the $20+ trillion of US equities owned by foreigners reflects price appreciation rather than underlying buying. For every $1 of US equities bought, roughly $10 of equities are now owned.

The US stock-dollar correlation has been negative for ten years, which gave foreign holders an incentive to leave US equity exposure unhedged. When an equity shock originates in the US, the correlation flips to positive, so USD losses add to equity losses.
A positive stock-dollar correlation can push foreign holders to hedge their stock of US assets, as seen around Liberation Day.

A USD-down, equity-down move should be validated by falling US real yields. The author says the main driver of the rates-higher, equities-higher move this year has been a large rise in capex expectations, so lower real yields and lower equities would be consistent with those expectations being cut.
The author takes no view on the AI ecosystem's outlook. The risks to the dollar are more two-sided than the market has priced over the last few weeks.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Falling real yields alongside falling equities and a falling dollar would indicate that AI capex expectations are being downgraded.

risk_factors: An AI-driven equity correction could coincide with dollar weakness instead of dollar strength.
Foreign hedging of the large stock of US equity holdings could add to dollar selling.
Foreign equity inflows currently finance the entire US current account deficit, and the equity market is highly concentrated.
vol_and_positioning: Foreign holders have kept US equity exposure largely unhedged for ten years because of the negative stock-dollar correlation. A flip to positive correlation in a US-centric equity shock could trigger hedging shifts, as around Liberation Day.

tension_points.bull_case: The dollar's historical negative correlation with US stocks has made it a risk-off asset, and foreign holders left their US equity exposure unhedged.
tension_points.bear_case: In a US-centric equity shock the dollar-equity correlation flips to positive, USD losses add to equity losses, and foreign hedging of US asset holdings can add to dollar selling.
tension_points.what_invalidates: US real yields rising while equities and the dollar fall would fail to validate the capex-downgrade dynamic.
